newsitem.title: UK: SOME N. SEA CRUDES WEAKEN, BRENT STEADY TO SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: SOME N. SEA CRUDES WEAKEN, BRENT STEADY TO SOFTER.

text.p: Some August loading North Sea crudes fell out of bed on Monday as prompt cargoes put pressure on the market and traded at much lower numbers, traders said.
Two Statfjord cargoes (loading Aug 15-17 and 16-18) traded at dated Brent +5 cents and +4 cents respectively. Two weeks ago the grade was trading some 20-25 cents higher.

"They are prompt cargoes but it is a good reflection that the buying is gone. But the price drop may have been overdone," one refiner said. Otherwise trade was limited though an end August Forties cargo was thought to have moved at a solid 30 cent premium to dated Brent.
Dated Brent was heard discussed steady to softer around September Brent -28/-20 cents, with one trader heard short for either one or two cargoes to cover a recent Polish tender.
Outright levels were basically unchanged with September Brent on the IPE down just two cents on the day at $18.46 a barrel by 1720 GMT.

Of the two August 26-28 Brent cargoes in Monday's chains, one was kept by BP and the other clocked to Spanish refiner Repsol. Traders said they expected the Repsol cargoes loading dates would be defered and it would thus be passed along the chains again.
Other grades lost ground with Ekofisk heard talked around dated Brent +15/20 cents.
CFD action was light with next week around October -35/-32 cents. The following two to three weeks were around steady to two cents in contango.

Traders said the upcoming Iraqi crude exports would not have as dramatic an effect on the market as some had expected. Much of the early barrels from Ceyhan will go transatlantic and the main effect would be on the Urals differential in the Mediterranean.
